c2fadc428199286f: A test account protected by "Password1" helped an intruder steal personal data relating to 3,300 people, mostly children, in a ransomware attack that has drawn regulatory rebukes for two Welsh organizations.
The Information Commission's Office (ICO) issued reprimands rather than fines to Ogi Networks Limited (ONL) and the Local Government Data Unit – Wales, also known as Data Cymru.
According to the ICO, altnet ONL provided server and connectivity infrastructure, licensing, and support to Data Cymru, which helps public bodies across Wales make effective use of data.

On November 1, 2024, Data Cymru suffered a ransomware attack after a miscreant exploited a test account called Test2 to infiltrate its network and encrypt 182.7 GB of data housed in a file server and an internal database server.
"Before deploying the ransomware, the threat actor exfiltrated 42 GB of data from a primary domain controller, a file server and an SQL server," the ICO said on Tuesday in its reprimand of ONL [PDF].
ONL told the ICO it created the test account on January 13, 2012, during its initial project for Data Cymru.

"ONL confirmed that the creation of the 'Test2' account was likely intended to test user account access before migrating 'real' users to its services," the ICO said. "When it was created, the 'Test2' account was given the password of 'Password1'."
The ICO cited Bitwarden's password strength tool, which rated "Password1" as "very weak" and estimated a cracking time of less than a second.

"The local administrator accounts on the three impacted systems all had the same password. This meant that once one system had been breached, the local account hashes could be collected and used by the threat actor to authenticate access to other systems on the Data Cymru network," the regulator added.

"ONL confirmed that it did not carry out any reviews of local administrator accounts following their initial deployment. This meant these accounts remained active, regardless of whether they were used, and continued to use the same default passwords set at the time of their creation in January 2012, as part of ONL's initial project with Data Cymru, for more than 12.5 years."

The data watchdog reprimanded ONL under Article 32 of the UK GDPR because it failed to put in place "appropriate technical and organisational measures" to ensure processing systems and services were safe, and it didn't regularly assess or evaluate those measures. It found ONL had no auditing procedures to review user accounts within Data Cymru's Active Directory.
The ICO's separate reprimand of Data Cymru [PDF] also detailed failures in its security arrangements.

"Password1 is not an appropriate password, it is a wide-open door to nefarious actors," said ICO head of investigations David Doodson. "This incident shows how a single weak password, attached to an account that was no longer needed, can leave the door open to a serious cyber-attack that can affect thousands.

"The responsibility for these failures did not sit with one organisation alone. ONL created the test account whilst Data Cymru retained overall control of its network, including the ability to instruct ONL to create or remove accounts. Neither had put in place sufficiently clear and effective measures to ensure that old accounts were routinely identified and removed." ®

fd38e3d0e3d7d54d: KUALA LUMPUR: The mini revival Leong Jun Hao was hoping for at the European swing has gone flat.
Japan's world No. 16 Koki Watanabe once again exposed world No. 31 Jun Hao's weaknesses, beating him 21-15, 21-11 in the first round of the French Open in Paris on Tuesday.
It was the Malaysian men's singles' second consecutive first-round exit after last week's Denmark Open.
And time is running out for Jun Hao to safeguard his place in the national squad.
He has failed to reach the last eight in 15 tournaments this year, losing in the first round in nine of them.
In retrospect, BAM performance committee chairman Datuk Seri Lee Chong Wei had given Jun Hao a second chance after the shuttler risked losing his national spot in June due to indiscipline.
However, little has changed in his overall performance, apart from a win over then world No. 1 Jonatan Christie of Indonesia during the team event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games last month.
That victory offered hope, but it was short-lived after Jun Hao suffered consecutive straight-game defeats to Watanabe, against whom he previously held the upper hand.
Earlier, Jun Hao had led Watanabe 4-1 in their head-to-head record, but the Japanese has now won their last three meetings to draw level.
Meanwhile, mixed doubles pair Jimmy Wong-Cheng Su Yin's inconsistency continued with a 22-20, 21-18 defeat to Indonesia's world No. 12 pair Amri Syahnawi-Nita Violina Marwah.
Former national mixed doubles head coach Nova Widianto formed the pair after Su Yin's partner Hoo Pang Ron left the national team to become an independent player.

Though world No. 41 Jimmy-Su Yin reached the semi-finals of the China Masters, Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing have been producing better results. Pang Ron-Pei Jing finished runners-up at the China Masters and reached the semi-finals of the Macau Open and Denmark Open last week.
The independent pair eye a deep run at the French Open, but they must first overcome China's world No. 26 Gao Jia Xuan-Wu Meng Ying in a tricky opening match tomorrow.
Meanwhile, world No. 42 Wong Tien Ci-Lim Chiew Sien bowed out after a 21-12, 21-10 defeat to Taiwan's world No. 30 Wu Guan Xun-Lee Chia Hsin on Tuesday.

128c0ed175f4386c: PETALING JAYA: Sebuah gabungan pertubuhan masyarakat sivil memberi amaran supaya pelarian tidak diambil tindakan serupa dengan pendatang asing tanpa izin (Pati).
CSO Platform for Reform berkata, tindakan menyeluruh besar-besaran terhadap kedua-dua kumpulan itu bukanlah langkah keselamatan kawalan sempadan sebaliknya mampu mengancam nyawa.

Kumpulan itu mengulas gesaan Ahli Parlimen Bersatu Radzi Jidin, supaya operasi besar-besaran seluruh negara diambil bagi menangkap pendatang tanpa izin, termasuk menggerakkan anggota tentera untuk membantu Jabatan Imigresen memberkas dan menghantar mereka pulang ke negara asal.

“Golongan pelarian melarikan diri daripada perang, penindasan dan pelanggaran hak asasi manusia. Menghantar mereka pulang ke negara asal tanpa menilai apa mereka perlukan dari segi perlindungan mampu mendedahkan mereka kepada penyeksaan, pemenjaraan malah juga maut,” katanya dalam kenyataan.
“Mengambil tindakan menyeluruh membangkitkan risiko yang meletakkan ribuan golongan lemah, termasuk wanita dan kanak-kanak dalam bahaya.”

Gabungan itu berkata, pelarian tidak boleh dianggap sebagai ancaman keselamatan hanya kerana tidak mempunyai dokumen imigresen, malah keadaaan mereka mesti dibezakan daripada kes melibatkan pemerdagangan dan penyeludupan manusia serta penipuan imigresen.

Terdahulu, bekas ahli Parlimen Klang Charles Santiago mengkritik Radzi kerana cuba ‘mencari publisiti’ apabila menggesa supaya operasi membanteras pendatang tanpa dokumen di seluruh negara dilaksanakan dengan melibatkan tentera.

Santiago berkata, pekerja migran bukan punca masalah Pati di negara ini, sebaliknya berpunca daripada ‘ketamakan, rasuah, pengambilan pekerja secara eksploitatif dan majikan yang tidak bertanggungjawab’
CSO Platform for Reform berkata, isu pendatang tanpa izin mesti ditangani menggunakan dokumentasi yang betul, penjejakan secara berkesan dan penguatkuasaan yang bertanggungjawab.
“Segelintir pendatang mungkin memasuki Malaysia menggunakan dokumen sah, yang kemudian hilang atau luput. Keadaan mereka mesti ditentukan sewajarnya,” kata kumpulan itu.
Kumpulan itu turut mengkritik cadangan supaya tentera dikerahkan dengan menegaskan tanggungjawab hakiki tentera adalah melindungi kedaulatan negara dan mengawal sempadan terhadap ancaman luar.
“Penguatkuasaan imigresen dan pengurusan pelarian memerlukan kakitangan yang berkelayakan khas, prosedur undang-undang jelas, serta perlindungan kemanusiaan sewajarnya.
“Tidak patut untuk menggunakan pendekatan penahanan serta pengusiran besar-besaran, dan pengerahan tentera juga tidak patut menggantikan pentadbiran imigresen yang berkesan,” menurut kumpulan itu.

Ia menggesa kerajaan mengukuhkan agensi awam, menyiasat sindiket pemerdagangan serta rasuah, memastikan majikan yang mengeksploitasi pekerja dipertanggungjawabkan, selain mewujudkan mekanisme telus bagi menilai keperluan perlindungan pelarian sebelum pengusiran dilaksanakan.

9490aefdbadaa272: SAN FRANCISCO: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have ordered more than three million of Nvidia's new RTX PRO 5500 graphics cards with a collective sticker price of over US$35 billion, two people familiar with the matter said, in a rush for a less powerful but export-compliant chip amid US restrictions on trade with China.

US-based chipmaker Nvidia has told customers and partners it cannot guarantee that it can fill the orders because demand from Chinese technology companies far exceeds planned production, the two sources and a third person familiar with the matter said. They requested anonymity because they are not authorised to speak to the media.

The RTX PRO 5500 is a workstation chip, designed for powerful professional computers rather than the large data-centre clusters that use Nvidia's most advanced AI processors. But it is among the most powerful Nvidia chips that are still available to Chinese buyers.

Nvidia's Blackwell-based B300 data-centre chip is not allowed to be sold to Chinese buyers under US export controls, while exports of its Hopper-based H200 are reviewed on a case-by-case basis and are subject to licensing conditions.

One source said Nvidia told partners they might receive only five per cent to 10 per cent of the quantities requested. Another said the company had indicated it could produce no more than 3 million RTX PRO 5500 cards globally in 2027. Total orders from customers in China have exceeded 6 million, two of the sources said.
The three Chinese tech giants' orders are for cards priced at about US$11,400 each, two of the sources said, giving them a potential combined value of more than US$35 billion.
The scale of the orders, which have not been previously reported, underscores the ongoing appetite among Chinese companies for Nvidia hardware despite the US curbs.

Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang has said the restrictions reduced Nvidia's share of China's AI data-centre chip market from a near monopoly to effectively nothing. But demand for the RTX PRO 5500 suggests Nvidia retains a sizeable potential market in China through less powerful products that may still be available.

The surge in demand also highlights how US restrictions have tightened computing-power supplies in the world's second-largest economy as Chinese companies race to develop cutting-edge AI models and propel Beijing's effort to deploy the technology across its industries.
Washington's curbs have pushed Chinese firms toward domestic suppliers, while Beijing has encouraged the use of homegrown chips.

Huawei, in particular, has gained market share, though Chinese chipmakers have generally struggled to match leading American products, partly because separate restrictions have limited access to the foreign equipment that is used to make the most advanced semiconductors.
An Nvidia spokesperson said Chinese producers of workstation chips and cards have experienced "unprecedented growth since 2022," when the curbs were first imposed.

"US firms continue to be restricted by a combination of outdated US export controls, which cover gaming products released nearly a half a decade ago, and China's own limit on US imports," the spokesperson said.
ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent did not respond to requests for comment.
The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees the export controls, and China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology did not respond to requests for comment.
AN EXPORT-COMPLIANT ALTERNATIVE
The RTX PRO 5500 is less powerful than Nvidia's H200 and B300 chips, which are designed to be linked in large numbers for the most demanding AI training and deployment workloads.

Chinese companies are seeking to use the cards primarily for AI inference, or running trained models to generate chatbot responses, the three sources said. Inference generally requires less computing power than training models on massive datasets.
The RTX PRO 5500 is similar to the RTX 6000D in performance, according to product specifications seen by Reuters.

Nvidia launched the RTX 6000D in the middle of last year as a reduced-capability product designed to meet US export restrictions. Major Chinese tech firms initially showed little interest, with some declining to place orders, Reuters reported last year.
At the time, buyers viewed the chips as overly expensive given their capabilities and hoped Washington would eventually allow sales of more powerful Nvidia processors.
Those expectations have faded as restrictions have remained in place and AI computing capacity has remained scarce, making the RTX PRO 5500 a more attractive substitute, two of the sources said.
SUPPLY SQUEEZE
Nvidia's inability to promise full deliveries reflects both a surge in demand and its manufacturing priorities, two of the sources said.

Starting in 2027, Nvidia is expected to devote much of its capacity at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co to Rubin, its next-generation platform for large-scale data centres, rather than products like the RTX PRO 5500, two of the sources said. TSMC declined to comment.
Nvidia has told customers to expect early samples in December, with commercial deliveries beginning in the first quarter of 2027, they added.
The RTX 6000D has since been discontinued and its market price in China has doubled, one of the sources said.
In an Oct 13 filing, Shenzhen-listed fintech and AI-computing services company Tansun Technology said it had agreed to buy 20,000 RTX PRO 5500 cards from an unidentified counterparty.
It cautioned that supply shortages, industry demand and overseas technology controls could delay deliveries or reduce volumes.

c7a7043d35fec3f5: WANGARATTA (Australia), Oct 20 — A rural Australian town felt a mix of horror and disbelief today after a highly respected lawmaker was gravely injured in what looked to be a targeted attack.
Former nurse and midwife Helen Haines entered parliament in 2019, earning respect across the political divide for her efforts to stamp out corruption and bolster transparency.
The 65-year-old was struck by a two-tonne SUV in Wangaratta yesterday afternoon, suffering critical injuries in what authorities described as a “deliberate” act of violence.
Wangaratta Mayor Irene Grant said a sombre mood had settled over the town of about 30,000 people, a regional hub about 250 kilometres northeast of state capital Melbourne.
“Helen was well respected. She was diligent and hard working,” Grant told AFP.
“What has happened to Helen has caused the community to step back in utter disbelief. We can’t believe it, people are horrified by what has happened.”
Haines — who lives on a small cattle property outside Wangaratta — was getting something from the trunk of her car when her alleged attacker drove past in a Toyota Land Cruiser.
Authorities said the 43-year-old man turned the car around before veering at Haines and pinning her against her own vehicle.
The driver then allegedly reversed before ramming her again, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said.
‘Devastated’
Police have said little about the alleged attacker’s motive.
Locals, meanwhile, are struggling to comprehend why anyone would wish harm on the well-liked Haines.
Florist Jess Woodrow said Haines was a friendly face who would pop into the store when she was not tied up in the capital Canberra.
“We are absolutely devastated to hear what has happened. Helen was a beautiful person. She didn’t have a bad bone in her body,” Woodrow told AFP.
“It’s the last thing you would think would happen here.”
Haines entered parliament as an independent lawmaker in 2019, representing the sprawling seat of Indi.
She was a popular representative, holding the seat at the 2025 election with a hefty margin of more than 18,000 votes.
Haines was a vocal champion for greater climate action, better rural healthcare, and help for struggling small businesses.
The First Peoples’ Assembly of Victoria said Haines was a “staunch supporter” of Indigenous rights as well.
But it was her work to hold politicians to account that perhaps earned Haines the most respect both inside and outside parliament.
“Helen Haines is characterised by her kindness, her compassion, her diligence, her intelligence,” Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said.
“She’s someone who is such a strong advocate and is widely respected right across the political spectrum because the way that she advocates is very respectful.” — AFP
f382bc1ee56d8f38: BOGOTÁ, Oct 20 — Ahead of an election that could return the right to power in Brazil, polls show support slipping for recently elected conservative leaders across Latin America.

New surveys in Peru, Colombia, Chile and Argentina suggest voters are losing patience with governments elected on promises to curb crime, revive weak economies and forge closer ties with US President Donald Trump.
Peru’s conservative President Keiko Fujimori and her hardline, gun-toting Colombian counterpart, Abelardo de la Espriella, are the latest newcomers to see their ratings fall.

An Ipsos poll last week showed approval of Fujimori dropping to 40 percent from 57 percent when she took office in August, while De la Espriella’s fell more than three points in his first month in office.

In Chile, where voters elected their most conservative president in three decades last year amid concerns over organized crime, one-quarter of President Jose Antonio Kast’s supporters say they regret backing him, according to the left-wing Fundacion Nodo XXI.
Argentine President Javier Milei, a hero to free-market conservatives across the region, has also seen his ratings hit record lows a year before seeking re-election.

“I think a lot of these governments raised expectations probably unrealistically. People want quick results, which are impossible to produce,” Michael Shifter, senior fellow at The Inter-American Dialogue think tank in Washington, told AFP.
But the backlash has little to do with ideology, he cautioned.
“I’m not sure that if these were governments of the left that it would be any different,” he said.

An AmericasBarometer survey of more than 25,000 people in 21 countries found weak support for the leaders of eight US allies that belong to Trump’s “Shield of the Americas” alliance: Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Guatemala, Panama and Paraguay.
‘Concrete action’
Nowhere is impatience for better governance more visible than in Bolivia, where voters dumped the long-ruling socialists in the midst of the country’s worst economic crisis in 40 years.
President Rodrigo Paz was elected as a moderate, pro-business alternative, but was only six months into his mandate when demonstrators demanding his resignation blockaded major cities.
Many blame the 59-year-old for failing to end crippling fuel shortages.
“I thought it would be different, that things were going to change,” Jamil Alanoca, a 19-year-old business student, told AFP.
Across the border in Peru, voters went to the polls in April and June seeking relief from an extortion epidemic and are already showing frustration at the lack of results.
“A problem that has persisted for so many years (insecurity) isn’t going to be solved overnight,” Guillermo Loli, director of opinion polls at Ipsos Peru, told AFP.
But “at least concrete actions should be seen,” he said.
The Bukele exception
Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele’s iron-fisted approach to his country’s gangs has earned him a cult-like following.

The self-described “world’s coolest dictator” enjoys approval of 83 percent, according to the AmericasBarometer survey, after driving crime rates to historic lows through a sweeping anti-gang crackdown.
The gains were achieved by jailing more than 90,000 suspects under a four-year-old state of emergency that rights groups say has been marked by serious abuses.

“Bukele’s El Salvador remains a defining experiment — a state that traded liberties for safety and, by these measures, delivered greater safety,” the 2026 Pulse of Democracy report produced by Vanderbilt University using AmericasBarometer polling said.
Shifter expressed doubt that Bukele’s success against domestic gangs could be replicated against the transnational crime networks operating elsewhere in the region.
“Bukele, I think, is really sui generis, he’s the exception,” he said.
Chilean pensioner Leoncio Silva said he believed that, given more time, Kast would vanquish the foreign gangs blamed for a surge in violence in his country.
“Let’s wait a year and see,” he urged. — AFP
0cc474777a4f8856: BARRANQUILLA (Colombia), Oct 20 — Colombia’s new right-wing leader has built himself a costly new presidential palace — a white-columned mansion far from Bogota that doubles as a political manifesto.

Tucked inside a Caribbean military base, President Abelardo de la Espriella’s new headquarters is meant to embody two of his signature promises: a focus on Colombia’s security forces and shifting power away from a capital accused of neglecting the country’s regions.
The austere neoclassical building, set amid tropical gardens and palm trees in Barranquilla, has quickly become one of the most visible symbols of his presidency.
Admirers see a bold statement of decentralisation from a leader determined to govern from beyond Bogota.
“For a very long time, the coast and the regions outside Bogota have been forgotten,” said Libardo Charris, a 54-year-old furniture merchant in Barranquilla.
The debate has even prompted questions about whether a city of about 1.3 million people is the new seat of power.
De la Espriella has frequently refers to Barranquilla as the “alternative capital.”
Critics dismiss it as an expensive political stage set that has earned the mocking nickname “the Temu White House.”

Constitutional experts say transforming Barranquilla into an official alternative seat of government would be difficult, although some Colombian presidents have occasionally governed from cities outside the capital.
“It is not an alternative capital. It is a place where the president stays for a few days and carries out his functions,” constitutional lawyer Juan Manuel Charry told AFP.
Creating a second capital would require constitutional reform and approval by Congress.
Political price tag
From the streets around the sprawling military compound, little of the mansion can be seen.
The property sits inside a restricted area of more than 50,000 square metres, roughly the size of several soccer fields.
A modest sign outside reads: “Presidency of the Republic. Freedom and Order.”
The mansion has already hosted high-profile visitors, including US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Costa Rican President Laura Fernandez.
Military personnel continue their daily routines around the complex, while official vehicles, aides and security details come and go.
The facilities include an underground bunker designed to shelter the president and senior civilian and military officials in a crisis.
An admirer of US President Donald Trump, De la Espriella has bristled at comparisons between his new base and the White House.
Yet social media has filled with memes highlighting the resemblance, while critics accuse him of embracing symbolism over substance.
De la Espriella often works from the compound dressed in tactical clothing, dark glasses and a baseball cap, blending into the military surroundings.
He arrives by helicopter or in convoys of armored vehicles, images regularly showcased on his social media accounts.
Recently he led a security operation in a nearby city carrying a pistol on his belt.
Better known as the hometown of pop star Shakira and for its carnival celebrations than as a center of political power, Barranquilla has found itself unexpectedly at the heart of national politics.
Gabriel Sanchez, a 47-year-old shopkeeper, said he welcomed the fact that Colombia’s Caribbean region was now receiving greater attention. Under De la Espriella, he said, the coast is “more visible.”
Street vendor Darlys Patricia Guerrero, 40, said it was “great” to have a presidential headquarters in the sweltering coastal city rather than the high-altitude capital.
“I’ve never seen the president around here,” she told AFP outside the Paradise Battalion base.

At a time of fiscal strain, opponents question the roughly US$650,000 (RM2.7 million) spent renovating the 1938 mansion, according to the Atlantico province’s governor, as well as the cost of moving presidential operations to Colombia’s Caribbean coast.
The criticism is pointed because De la Espriella, a wealthy former lawyer, won office promising a hard line against crime, a defense of traditional values and a leaner state.
Opponents argue that true decentralization requires transferring resources and decision-making powers to the regions rather than relocating the president’s desk.

“There are two governments: the one shown to the cameras and another behind it that we see in the territories,” said Edwin Capaz Lectamo, an Indigenous leader from the southwestern department of Cauca.
Yet beyond the legal questions, political arguments and online jokes, the Barranquilla headquarters has revived a long-running rivalry between Colombia’s Caribbean coast and the Andean capital.
“There’s more joy, more spontaneity here,” said homemaker Alejandra Diaz, 38, comparing her city with Bogota.

Whether it proves a lasting shift in how Colombia is governed or simply a costly symbol, the white-columned mansion has already achieved one thing: turning a building into a national debate about where power belongs. — AFP

ff47542fdb607803: PETALING JAYA: Umno Youth chief Dr Akmal Saleh defamed DAP vice-chairman Teresa Kok by accusing her of repeatedly undermining national harmony and subjecting her to personal insults over her criticism of a proposed halal certification policy, the Melaka High Court stated.
Judicial commissioner Isa Aziz Ibrahim said Akmal’s remarks went beyond legitimate political debate and carried a serious defamatory implication against Kok.

“The said video did carry a severe defamatory sting that the plaintiff habitually and continually destabilises national harmony,” he said in his grounds of judgment dated Oct 19 when ruling on Kok's defamation suit against Akmal.

The case stems from a video Akmal posted on TikTok, Facebook and Instagram in September 2024 after Kok questioned a proposal to make halal certification compulsory for restaurants and food businesses that did not serve pork or alcohol.

Kok had warned that the proposal could burden businesses, particularly smaller operators. Akmal responded by calling her an “old nyonya,” telling her to keep quiet, and suggesting that a “non-halal” label be placed on her forehead.
The judge rejected Akmal’s defence of fair comment, saying there was no factual basis for his allegation that Kok habitually disrupted national harmony.
“A defendant cannot invent or extrapolate unproven facts and comment upon them,” he said.
Isa also rejected Akmal’s claim of qualified privilege, citing the wide dissemination of the remarks and the personal attacks against Kok.
He noted that Akmal admitted recording the video in anger without seeking clarification, and that his primary motive was to attack Kok personally.
Akmal also kept the video online and neither apologised nor retracted his remarks.
The court also dismissed the argument that Kok had provoked the dispute through her Facebook post.
“An imperfect translation or unfortunate word choice by an elected official is not a licence for an opponent to execute an unevidenced character assassination,” Isa said.
The judge awarded Kok RM250,000 in general and aggravated damages.

He also ordered Akmal to remove the video from his social media accounts within seven days, barred him from republishing the defamatory remarks or words to the same effect, and ordered him to pay RM50,000 in costs.

ae74a8939d7a36bf: Google Cloud has blamed a “power event” for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe, and is pledging to restore normal service within the hour.
The unplanned downtime for customers began at 0608 UTC when europe-west-2-b, one of three local availability zones in the London region, started playing up.

According to an update on its status page, Google Cloud said at 1158 UTC that full recovery workloads should be “completed, tentatively” by 1300 UTC. Customers can expect another update at that point, with Google either giving the thumbs up, thumbs sideways or having to admit engineers are still working on a fix.

Services that went AWOL included BigQuery Data TransferService, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, Google Cloud NetApp Volumes, Google Kubernetes Engine, and Managed Service for Apache Kafka.
So what caused online services to melt at customers including Lloyds Bank, HSBC, Royal Mail, Rightmove, DPD, BT, Cloudflare, Screwfix and Revolut? Power.

"A power event caused an outage within europe-west2-b zone. The power event is mitigated. We are seeing the recovery of services and are prioritizing the recovery of existing workloads.Customers may not be able to yet create new workloads."
The Register has asked Google for further elucidation but it said the only information is available on the status page.

The "fragility" of the cloud model is again on display, Dr Amro Al-Said Ahmad, a lecturer in computer science at Keele University told The Register. He estimates that a total of 38 services were down and out for the count.

"The incident highlights the dependency effect of modern cloud ecosystems. When a core cloud region experiences failures, the impact extends far beyond the directly affected services. Applications, APIs, databases, authentication systems, payment platforms, analytics pipelines, and third-party SaaS products that depend on those services can all experience cascading failures."

"A problem in a single cloud region can therefore propagate through an entire digital supply chain, affecting organisations that are several layers removed from the original outage. While this is a regional outage centered on europe-west2, the breadth of affected services highlights a key cloud engineering lesson: resilience is not achieved by simply moving to the cloud. True resilience requires designing for regional failures through multi-region deployments, workload portability, and tested disaster recovery procedures." ®

In updates on Sunday and Monday evening, NEA warned that this could happen from as early as tonight.

ea6e97a021c2241c: PUTRAJAYA: The Higher Education Ministry and Universiti Malaya (UM) have no intention of taking action against the student who went viral recently after asking a "tough" question during the i-Future programme.

Commenting on allegations of threats, abuse and condemnation directed at the student, Zambry said such behaviour should not occur and advised the student to lodge a police report to enable an investigation.
He urged the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission to examine the posts and accounts involved, including the possibility that fake accounts had been used.
"If anyone has attempted to engage in wrongdoing, the student concerned should take appropriate action by lodging a report with the relevant authorities," he said.

"I also urge everyone not to turn students into weapons of political propaganda, to the extent that they become victims of certain agendas.

b89f632339a76df8: PETALING JAYA: PKR menuntut Presiden Pejuang, Mukhriz Mahathir memohon maaf kerana mendakwa rancangan untuk menggantung dan membatalkan pendaftaran Perikatan Nasional (PN) dibentangkan dalam Kongres Nasional PKR pada Ogos lalu.

bb29353e5da58eed: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is encouraging the public to use TuJu, a locally developed navigation application created by the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA), as an alternative for road navigation.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the alternative was proposed due to security concerns over information and data on citizens' movements, given that the Waze application is subject to Israeli laws.

He said the matter was among the topics discussed at the third meeting of the National Cyber Security Committee, which he chaired today to review evolving cyber threats and strengthen the nation's preparedness and digital sovereignty.

"Also discussed were the implementation of the Cyber Security Act 2024, the security of MyDigital ID, preparations to counter threats from quantum computing through post-quantum cryptography (PQC), emerging threats involving autonomous artificial intelligence, and the protection of National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII).

"We cannot compromise when it comes to the security of our citizens' data and identities. Therefore, the government is strengthening an integrated identity ecosystem utilising MyKad as a physical credential and MyDigital ID for digital transactions, supported by more robust cyber protections, including preparations for future threats via PQC," he said in a Facebook post.

The prime minister said these efforts were crucial to ensuring that the digitalisation of public services continued to benefit the people without compromising security, public trust or national sovereignty.

Like many online services, Muse allows users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. A single query is all that's required

c2b2ba6c286efd9f: BANGKOK: A Thai appeals court overturned on Tuesday a conviction for the attempted rape of a teenage girl handed to the country's first Olympic gold medallist, but upheld his sentence for abduction.
Somluck Kamsing, now 53, became a national hero in Thailand when he won featherweight boxing gold at the 1996 Olympics in Atlanta.
He was found guilty in January 2025 of abduction for indecent purposes and attempted rape of a person aged between 15 and 18, and sentenced to just over three years in prison.
A regional appeals court in Khon Kaen dismissed the attempted rape conviction on Tuesday, saying the victim's testimony contained "inconsistencies" and there was no evidence of coercion or threats.
Somluck's sentence was adjusted to two years, the court said in a media statement.
A 17-year-old girl filed a complaint against Somluck in December 2023, saying he had assaulted her in a hotel in Khon Kaen, a city in Thailand's northeast.
The court said on Tuesday the pair met in a bar and she went back to his hotel on his motorcycle.
Somluck, who also won boxing titles at the 1994 and 1998 Asian Games in Hiroshima and Bangkok respectively, denied the allegations.

3d3a13a195c627dc: OSLO, Oct 20 — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Oslo today for talks with top US envoys in a bid to get strained relations with Washington “on a more constructive path”, Oslo said.
“We are maintaining all contacts that can help bring peace,” Zelensky said in a social media post announcing his arrival in Oslo.

US-led diplomatic efforts to end Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II have stalled in recent months, as Washington has shifted focus towards the war with Iran.
The Norway talks were due to begin this afternoon and continue into the evening, Store told reporters.
“The aim is to put diplomatic efforts on a more constructive path,” he said.

Ahead of the meeting, Zelensky today said he held “substantive” and “constructive” talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in which he insisted that the US military satellite system Ukraine uses, Starshield, “needs to be restored” and that ballistic missile interceptors “are needed to protect lives”.

Zelensky told US senators yesterday that “the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles” already paid for by European countries, and that the shipment was waiting for US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s signature.
He said several European countries were ready to transfer Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles but were still awaiting US approval.
The United States has denied making any changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine, and Rubio today said Washington was not deliberately withholding supplies.
“There’s nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine,” Rubio said while on a trip to India.
“It’s simply, it’s a balance between our obligations to other partners and frankly our own... requirements for our own facilities as well.”

Trump has also denied ordering a reduction in speeds on the US government-owned and -controlled Starshield network after Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX developed it, said the order could only have come from the White House.
Strained relations

“Zelensky doesn’t know what he’s talking about,” Trump said yesterday.
“To be honest, I think it’s time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine.”

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed earlier that “the topic of such a hypothetical has indeed been mentioned” when asked about a Wall Street Journal report on Sunday that Trump, Putin and Xi could meet.
Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga said that such a meeting would “only encourage Putin to continue this war”.

e991eca885f8eb35: Bullhorn is the latest tech giant finding itself on the wrong end of a cyberattack, forcing the recruitment software provider to shut down its platform while it investigates.

The US-based company, which serves more than 10,000 customers worldwide, says its systems are now back online in the UK, US, and Australia. Unfortunately for customers hoping to get back to work, online doesn't necessarily mean working.

In its latest status update, published on Tuesday, Bullhorn confirmed that some users were still struggling with single sign-on (SSO), password resets, and customizations, while several products continued to report degraded performance.

Things started going sideways on Friday, October 16, when Bullhorn flagged problems getting job postings onto Indeed. By the following morning, the platform was suffering a full-blown outage, and Bullhorn confirmed later that day that it was dealing with something rather more serious than a technical hiccup.

"We have detected a cyber incident on the Bullhorn Platform. We have temporarily disabled access to our systems in order to contain the activity while we investigate further," the company said, noting that it had roped in cybersecurity specialists from CrowdStrike to help investigate the attack and restore its services.
For recruitment agencies using Bullhorn, the outage meant losing access to candidate records, job applications, placements and, in some cases, the systems used to get people paid.

Services began returning on Monday, but recovery has been anything but seamless. As of Tuesday morning, Bullhorn's status page still listed degraded performance across several products, including its automation tools, Talent Platform, Onboarding365 and Time & Expense.

While Bullhorn is making progress getting customers back into their accounts, it has yet to answer arguably the bigger question: whether the attackers stole anything. In its customer FAQ, it said a forensic investigation is ongoing, and has not yet determined whether attackers exfiltrated customer data.

Bullhorn says it will contact affected customers if the investigation finds their information was compromised, and it also warned people to watch out for opportunistic crooks looking to exploit the chaos.

"Threat actors may pose as Bullhorn personnel via email, text, or phone calls, using the incident as a pretext to request credentials or sensitive information," it warned on Tuesday, stressing that its employees would never ask customers to disclose passwords, multi-factor authentication codes, or verification tokens.
The company has also required password resets for users who don’t log in through SSO, while customers using API integrations have been instructed to rotate their credentials.

The cause of the intrusion remains unknown, and Bullhorn has not publicly identified the attackers or confirmed whether ransomware was involved. The company didn’t respond to The Register’s questions at publication time.
The outage may be coming to an end, but Bullhorn's investigation into what the attackers actually did is far from over. ®

678424bafb0509cf: The current narrative around artificial intelligence in the workplace is largely driven by Silicon Valley. But treating the tech sector as an island misses the actual trends in technology adoption–tech is just the first industry in line.

As generative AI and automation tools mature, the shifts currently reshaping software engineering and product management will inevitably filter into healthcare, education, retail, and manufacturing. The variation in adoption rates today isn’t a sign that non-tech industries are falling behind, but rather a reflection of the different speeds at which industries absorb new workflows. For leaders and their teams outside of tech, this differential pace provides a practical blueprint for how AI adoption unfolds, and where the opportunities lie.
The AI adoption spectrum by industry
Recent survey data from TripleTen highlights just how stark the current adoption curve is across different sectors of the economy (see Figure 1).
Figure 1: The AI adoption curve remains steep across industries, but non-tech industry adoption rates are increasing.

While tech leads the way, finance emerges as a clear second: 48% of finance workers have been asked to use AI chatbots, and 32% have been asked to automate parts of their workflow. This demonstrates how rapidly knowledge work integrates AI once clear use cases emerge.

By contrast, sectors like healthcare (18% asked to use chatbots) and education (25%) reflect lower initial exposure. Because these broad industry categories encompass a mix of specialized hands-on professionals, clinical or instructional personnel, and back-office administrative staff, universal adoption was never going to happen overnight. Integrating automated tools into compliance-heavy or human-facing operations requires a more deliberate pace, which is reflected by the lower numbers.
The AI skills workers are being asked to learn

Across all surveyed industries, 79% of workers report being asked to learn at least one skill they didn’t previously have. Looking at the specific competencies demanded in tech today offers a preview of the skill sets likely to shift into other sectors (see Figure 2).
Figure 2: Workforces across industries are learning new skills.

Although some of these sound like niche skills confined to tech, many of them will translate to frontline work across sectors—from hospital systems managing patient logistics to school districts processing administrative reporting.

One skill gets less attention than it should. Only 30% of managers and owners call judging whether AI output is right or wrong an absolute must, which puts it sixth on a list of seven. As AI tools reach more industries, this is the skill that catches mistakes before they cause problems. It is also where work experience helps most: To spot a wrong answer, you need to know what the right one looks like.
How early AI adoption helps your career

Early AI adoption offers clear professional leverage: TripleTen’s survey data shows that when managers learned a new skill or automation process from an employee, 88% of those employee-led AI innovations became standard company practice.

In early-adopting industries, employees who identify repetitive administrative tasks and use AI tools to streamline them have a voice in shaping organizational policy. As healthcare networks, educational institutions, and retail operations begin broader rollouts of AI-enabled software, workers who understand how to validate outputs, prompt models, and automate routine tasks will hold a strong advantage. Being the person who can streamline administrative overhead promises better chances for retention, promotions, and wage growth.

Ana Riabova, the AI strategy and enablement lead at TripleTen, says, “Everyone talks about saving time, but the real win with early adoption is expanding what you can actually do. People who get ahead are using it to handle things they used to have to hand off. It doesn’t matter how senior or junior you are. You keep your core skills, but suddenly you aren’t boxed in by them anymore.”
The AI resource gap: Who pays for training and how workers learn

If non-tech industries absorb these tools more gradually, the challenge for workers lies in getting access to quality learning resources. Workers’ out-of-pocket investment in training varies significantly by industry:
Tech: $1,758 average (13% spent $0)
Finance: $1,664 average (24% spent $0)
Healthcare: $990 average (45% spent $0)
Education: $883 average (42% spent $0)

Nearly half of healthcare and education workers spent nothing out of pocket on professional development last year. Furthermore, tech workers actively leverage a larger variety of learning channels (see Figure 3).
Figure 3: Professional development efforts mirror the AI adoption curve.

Tech workers are nearly twice as likely as all workers to use AI chatbots as learning tools (48% vs. 27%), and more than twice as likely as workers outside tech (21%), effectively using AI to accelerate their acquisition of other skills.

However, ask workers whom they trust most to teach them a new job skill, and they choose someone currently doing that job (31%). Fewer pick an official certification program (19%), an AI tool (16%), or a university professor (6%).
Conclusion

The difference in AI adoption rates across industries is not a story of who is succeeding and who is failing. Rather, it’s a timeline of how technology diffuses through an economy. Tech and finance are testing the mechanics of AI integration today. For workers in healthcare, education, retail, and manufacturing, the current phase provides a valuable window to observe which skills generate real productivity gains—allowing them to build those competencies before they become standard industry expectations.
This content was produced by TripleTen. It was not written by MIT Technology Review’s editorial staff.
682435d42d6d5ab0: LONDON: Britain will fly Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets on defensive missions to help protect Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure from Houthi aerial attacks, the Ministry of Defence said on Tuesday.

The ministry said the aircraft would operate only in a defensive role and would not conduct offensive strikes against the Iran-aligned Houthis, whose attacks Britain says threaten regional stability and risk disrupting energy supplies and trade routes.

"The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable. The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate the situation in the region," defence minister Wes Streeting said in a statement.
"That’s why today I have approved further UK military support. RAF Typhoons will fly defensive air missions to help protect Saudi airspace from drones and missiles."
The additional support follows a request from Saudi Arabia's government, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier this month Britain was prepared to consider.

Britain will also deploy an Atlas A400M transport aircraft and military advisers, expanding assistance announced in September which included an RAF Voyager air-to-air refuelling aircraft but not fighter jets.
Houthi attacks against Saudi oil facilities and other infrastructure have intensified in recent weeks as the conflict in Yemen has escalated.
Inside Yemen, authorities said a Houthi strike on Monday against a training camp for Saudi-backed government security forces killed 58 people.
e7b464755de85f60: KUALA LUMPUR: Seorang Ahli Parlimen Barisan Nasional (BN) mempersoalkan tindakan pemimpin DAP membuat laporan kepada Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM) berkaitan perbelanjaan Kementerian Kemajuan Desa dan Wilayah (KKDW), di sebalik penjelasan Perbendaharaan.

Mengulas tindakan Chong Zhemin (PH-Kampar) membuat laporan kepada SPRM berhubung peruntukan bagi projek jalan luar bandar bawah KKDN, Isam Isa (BN-Tampin) berkata Perbendaharaan mengesahkan bahawa 'isu teknikal penyelarasan' itu telah pun selesai.
"Tetapi kenapa DAP masih gian untuk membuat laporan pada 6 Oktober 2026?" soalnya di Dewan Rakyat, ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027.
Pada 6 Okt lalu, Chong menggesa SPRM menyiasat peranan Menteri Zahid Hamidi berhubung perbezaan RM2.1 bilion antara peruntukan dan perbelanjaan bagi projek jalan luar bandar itu.

Laporan Chong itu dibuat selepas Timbalan Ketua Setiausaha Perbendaharaan (Dasar) Zamzuri Abdul Aziz pada 1 Okt lalu menjelaskan isu dakwaan KKDW 'berbelanja melebihi peruntukan' sudah selesai. Tetapi beliau tidak memperincikan penyelesaian berkenaan.
Isam berkata 'penyelarasan peruntukan' merupakan perkara biasa dalam pengurusan kewangan awam, sambil merujuk kepada kenyataan Zamzuri.
Beliau juga berharap Kementerian Kewangan membentangkan kepada Dewan Rakyat tentang kementerian-kementerian lain yang melakukan 'penyelarasan peruntukan' supaya DAP boleh membuat laporan kepada SPRM.
"Ini bukan lagi soal ketelusan, ini jelas merupakan satu lagi gimik politik murahan DAP untuk membina persepsi buruk terhadap kepimpinan KKDW," katanya.
DAP dan Barisan Nasional berada dalam blok pemerintah. Zahid merupakan pengerusi BN, presiden Umno, dan timbalan perdana menteri.
Zahid sebelum ini menafikan KKDW berbelanja melebihi peruntukan diluluskan, menegaskan kementeriannya berbelanja mengikut jumlah yang diluluskan kerajaan atau dinyatakan dalam belanjawan.

Penafian itu dibuat selepas Ketua Setiausaha Perbendaharaan Johan Mahmood Merican memaklumkan KKDW sejak beberapa tahun lalu membuat komitmen dan berbelanja melebihi peruntukan tahunan diluluskan bagi projek jalan luar bandar.
Dalam pada itu, Isam menyifatkan serangan terhadap Umno dan BN sama ada di dalam mahupun di luar Dewan Rakyat sebagai sesuatu yang dijangka menjelang PRN Melaka dan PRU16.

Beliau turut mengkritik RSN Rayer (DAP-Jelutong) berhubung gesaan supaya peguam negara meneliti semula pertuduhan berkaitan rasuah yang melibatkan dana Yayasan Akalbudi, mengingatkan akan gesaan memisahkan peranan peguam negara daripada pendakwa raya.

Pada 4 Sept 2023, Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur melepaskan tanpa membebaskan Zahid daripada semua 47 pertuduhan pecah amanah, rasuah, dan pengubahan wang haram yang berkaitan dengan dana Yayasan Akalbudi.

Hakim Collin Lawrence Sequerah membuat keputusan itu selepas membenarkan permohonan oleh Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Dusuki Mokhtar untuk melepaskan tanpa membebaskan Zahid, apabila pihak pendakwaan memutuskan untuk memberhentikan prosiding kerana berhasrat menyiasat kes itu dengan lebih mendalam.

Isam turut menyentuh mengenai persaingan politik menjelang PRN Melaka, mengatakan BN yakin mampu mengukuhkan kedudukan susulan perkembangan di Johor dan Negeri Sembilan, yang meyaksikan kemenangan BN pada PRN yang diadakan.
Beliau berpesan kepada Pengerusi Pakatan Harapan (PH) Negeri Sembilan, Aminuddin Harun, supaya tidak memandang mudah kekuatan BN.

"Saya cuma mahu mengingatkan, janganlah terlalu mendabik dada dan 'berangan-angan Mat Jenin'. 'Gelombang Biru' telah pun terbukti kukuh di bumi Johor dan Negeri Sembilan. Insya-Allah, Melaka juga bakal dibirukan," katanya.

0c4ef484ce9458cc: IPOH, Oct 20 — A local woman suffered losses of more than RM129,000 after being duped by a non-existent online part-time job offer.
Kampar District Police Chief Supt Mohamad Nazri Daud said that his department received a report yesterday from the 34-year-old victim.

“Initial police investigations found that the victim saw an offer for a part-time job related to hotel bookings through social media. Interested, the victim left her phone number to be contacted by the party offering the job.

“The victim received a message from an unknown individual offering the job. The victim was then added to a WhatsApp group supposedly for handling online hotel booking transactions,” he said in a statement today.

Mohamad Nazri said the victim was instructed to make payments for each hotel booking into several bank accounts provided by the suspect, who promised that the capital would be returned along with a commission ranging between 10 to 20 percent, which would increase according to the transaction amount.
He said that due to being lured by the offer and the promise of profits, the victim carried out several money transfer transactions to eight accounts provided by the suspect.
“The victim began to realise she had been cheated when the promised capital and commission were not received after the payments were made. The victim suffered a loss of RM129,975.54,” he said.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama
523c557b4d931009: PETALING JAYA: While welcoming the move to centralise express bus ticket sales at licensed terminals, the Malaysian Public Transport Users Association (4PAM) warned that it could create a monopoly without proper government oversight.

Its president Ajit Johl said that to improve accountability, the transport ministry and the Land Public Transport Agency (Apad) must monitor service standards, system reliability, transaction charges, refunds and complaints.
“We should not replace a fragmented system with a monopoly which passengers have no alternative but to accept,” he said.
Ajit said passengers had long struggled to establish who was responsible when problems arose over bookings, cancellations and refunds.
In a circular, Apad gave licensed express bus terminals full control over ticket sales and trip management, with digital platform charges to be borne by bus operators rather than passengers.
Tickets may still be sold through online platforms or operators’ websites if the operators owned the terminals outright.
Ajit also called for competition among technology providers and warned against hidden payment gateway, processing and convenience fees.
He said all compulsory charges should be disclosed before passengers made their bookings, while clear standards were needed for refunds, complaint resolution and system failures.
He further urged the authorities to use the centralised system to introduce passenger manifests for every express bus journey.

"This is perhaps one of the biggest safety opportunities arising from the new system. Every legitimate passenger travelling on an express bus should be recorded against the specific bus operator, route and departure."
He said such records would help authorities identify passengers during accidents, notify their next of kin and verify insurance or compensation claims.

4a1532d84e6b6dc3: KUALA LUMPUR: Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Perak, Pahang and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, will operate as usual tomorrow, with outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze.
In NEGRI SEMBILAN, the state Education Department said in a statement today that all educational institutions under the Education Ministry (MOE) would operate as usual.
However, the Final Academic Session Exam (UASA) scheduled during this period must be postponed and rescheduled by the respective schools.

The postponement also applies to all internal school examinations, in line with the MOE's statement dated Oct 15. All outdoor activities must be suspended if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100.

In MELAKA, SELANGOR, PUTRAJAYA and KUALA LUMPUR, school administrators were instructed to monitor API readings issued by the Department of Environment and pay particular attention to pupils at higher risk.
In PAHANG, the state Education Department said schools in Rompin, Bentong and Cameron Highlands would operate tomorrow, but all outdoor activities would be suspended.
Schools in other districts would operate as usual, with any changes to be announced through the respective district education offices.
The PERAK Education Department urged everyone to remain alert to developments and heed the authorities' advice on the haze.
In PENANG, the state Education Department encouraged pupils to drink sufficient water and instructed schools to ensure an adequate supply of drinking water.
Pupils and school staff are also encouraged to wear face masks as a precaution, particularly those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups.

The education departments in Melaka, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Perak and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, have also given parents and guardians who are concerned about their children's health the option of keeping them at home, provided they inform the school.

Earlier, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek was reported as saying that decisions on school closures due to haze were made jointly by the Education Ministry, Health Ministry and Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), based on their respective areas of expertise.
She said the decisions took into account air quality monitoring and health risks to students, as well as the impact on learning if schools were closed for too long.

Meanwhile, Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, called on the government, private sector and local communities to take proactive steps and collective action to address the physical and psychological effects of haze on students and their families.

In a royal message posted on the official Facebook page of Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar last night, Her Majesty also emphasised community cooperation in strengthening Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR), as well as long-term strategic planning to deal with haze.
389d7d74dd3aa26e: PETALING JAYA: Pemimpin Bersama Rafizi Ramli mendakwa Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim mengelak daripada menangani isu lebih besar berhubung dakwaan kewujudan 'mafia korporat' yang dikaitkan dengan Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM).

Rafizi menzahirkan rasa kecewa terhadap respons Anwar terhadap soalan mengenai isu itu di Dewan Rakyat hari ini, menegaskan bahawa dakwaan berkenaan bukan sekadar tuduhan rasuah atau salah guna kuasa biasa.

"Skandal mafia korporat merujuk kepada pendedahan-pendedahan bahawa ada kumpulan di agensi penguatkuasaan, iaitu SPRM dan polis, yang dituduh bersekongkol dengan sekumpulan ahli perniagaan untuk mengugut ahli-ahli perniagaan lain menyerahkan syarikat-syarikat mereka.
"Tuduhan mengenai mafia korporat ini adalah luar biasa kerana ia mempersoalkan sama ada kumpulan jenayah haram telah menyusupi agensi penguatkuasaan.

Terdahulu, Anwar memberitahu Dewan Rakyat, kerajaan mewarisi sistem yang tidak telus yang membenarkan jenayah korporat serta manipulasi pasaran berlarutan tanpa sekatan selama berdekad-dekad.

Beliau berkata, kelemahan sistem terdahulu menyebabkan tindakan penguatkuasaan jarang diambil dalam kes berprofil tinggi membabitkan kerugian berbilion ringgit, termasuk pengambilalihan korporat dan transaksi perbankan yang didakwa dipengaruhi campur tangan politik.
Anwar turut mendakwa beberapa kes berkaitan kegiatan yang digelar mafia korporat mempunyai kaitan dengan seorang bekas menteri kewangan berpengaruh yang menguasai sumber kewangan besar.

Pada masa sama, beliau menafikan dakwaan bahawa seorang menteri menerima RM9.5 juta daripada seorang ahli perniagaan, menyifatkannya sebagai kenyataan berunsur politik yang tidak berasas. Tambahnya, menteri itu telah membawa perkara itu ke mahkamah.
Walaupun Anwar tidak menamakan menteri terbabit, individu yang dituduh menerima RM9.5 juta itu ialah Menteri Sumber Manusia R Ramanan.
Bagaimanapun, Rafizi mempersoalkan sama ada Ramanan benar-benar memulakan sebarang tindakan mahkamah, memandangkan tiada sebarang laporan berhubung perkara tersebut setakat ini.
d2548971ae12420b: PETALING JAYA: Higher education minister Zambry Abd Kadir has defended a Universiti Malaya (UM) student who questioned a fundraiser for Najib Razak, saying she would not face action from his ministry or the university.

In a TikTok video posted today, Zambry also urged the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to examine social media posts and accounts involved in the backlash against Ummi Umairah Bakhit, including whether fake accounts were being used.
“Some are saying that this student has been intimidated, threatened, verbally abused and so on,” he said in his video.
He said such intimidation was unacceptable, adding that Ummi could lodge a police report to enable the authorities to investigate.
“I want to stress that she has the right to speak. I hope freedom of expression can be exercised responsibly, respectfully and based on facts,” he said.
Zambry also cautioned political figures against using the student as a tool for propaganda, saying she risked becoming a victim of political agendas.
He also claimed that some ministers had called for T-shirts featuring Ummi to be made.

Ummi, an economics undergraduate, drew widespread attention at the International Young Future Leaders Summit in Kuala Lumpur after she questioned donations to help Najib pay a court-imposed fine of RM50 million.

During a dialogue with former youth and sports minister Khairy Jamaluddin, Selangor menteri besar Amirudin Shari and Johor menteri besar Onn Hafiz Ghazi, she asked how future leaders could oppose corruption while people were donating to the fundraiser.
Last Saturday, UM vice-chancellor Noor Azuan Abu Osman said no disciplinary action had been taken against Ummi and that students should be given room to express their views.
e351fbb2a2c9c7f6: LISBON: Portuguese police on Tuesday clashed with housing protesters in a dawn raid as they dismantled tent camps in the capital Lisbon, arresting 55 people.
Demonstrators in Portugal are protesting soaring housing costs, seeking to align themselves with similar actions in neighbouring Spain, where tents have been set up in central Madrid for weeks.
The weekend violence that flared in France on the sidelines of peaceful cost-of-living protests has raised alarm that the mayhem could spread to other countries with similar grievances.
Following a Saturday demonstration, dozens of tents were set up in Lisbon's central Rossio square.
As the police moved in on Tuesday morning, protesters formed a human chain before clashes broke out, according to footage broadcast by local television stations.
"The individuals taken into custody were brought to police facilities and will be brought before the competent judicial authority as soon as possible," the police said in a statement.
Law enforcement authorities, who also seized "228 camping structures," concluded that the gatherings were no longer legal.
The protesters accuse the government of failing to act to tackle Portugal's housing crisis, and trying to push through rental market reforms that will make eviction easier.
According to the protesters, some 30 demonstrators were injured and arrested on Tuesday.
Some protesters vowed to try to set up the camp again in the coming hours.
A large police presence was deployed on Tuesday morning in the city centre.
In Porto, where the movement began earlier this month, demonstrators dismantled their camp themselves in the face of threats of a police intervention.
The nearly four weeks of protests in Spain that erupted after the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her lifelong home led to the calling of a snap general election for Nov 29.
fc28b89bf72745fb: PUTRAJAYA: Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis recorded the highest rates of drug or substance addiction and abuse in the country, based on statistics up to June 2026, said National Anti-Drugs Agency (NADA) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh.
He said Terengganu recorded the highest rate at 735 people per 100,000 population, followed by Kelantan (694), Kedah (669) and Perlis (646).
"The ranking of these four states reflects the extent of drug addiction and abuse that requires attention and targeted intervention.

"Geographical factors also contribute to this situation, with cross-border smuggling routes identified as among the risk factors influencing drug-related problems in these areas," he said in a statement today.
Ruslin said a total of 130,307 drug and substance abuse cases were recorded nationwide during the same period, equivalent to a rate of 381 individuals per 100,000 population.
He said the statistics were compiled based on integrated data from four main sources, namely Nada, the police, Health Ministry and private rehabilitation centres.

In this regard, Ruslin said Nada was focusing on enforcement, prevention programmes and community empowerment in high-risk states, targeting three main segments, namely, educational institutions, families and communities.

"A total of 242 prevention and public awareness programmes were conducted, involving 16,408 participants overall, including 228 programmes in Terengganu, Kelantan and Kedah, which involved more than 16,000 participants," he said.
He added that 4,253 enforcement operations had been conducted nationwide, with 30,157 people detained for treatment and rehabilitation programmes as of last Sunday.

On treatment and rehabilitation, Ruslin said Nada prioritised a voluntary approach, with the average number of people seeking treatment on their own initiative rising from 75 a month in 2025 to 232 a month this year.
"This increase reflects positive progress following the implementation of amendments to the Drug Dependants (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Act 1983, which came into force on Aug 22, 2025," he said.

He said Nada would continue to adopt a data-driven approach and strengthen cooperation with state governments through the Drug Eradication Action Council (MTMD) meetings to coordinate prevention, treatment and rehabilitation efforts involving various agencies, families, educational institutions and communities.

42e9513caa2024a6: MELBOURNE: Australian police charged a man on Tuesday over what they alleged was a "targeted" attack with a vehicle on independent lawmaker Helen Haines.
Haines is fighting for her life in a hospital in Melbourne after being struck on Monday near her office in the town of Wangaratta, just over 200km northeast of the Victoria state capital.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has led an outpouring of support for Haines, who was widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption.

Her attack has also sparked soul-searching in a country where political violence is rare but where police have documented a steady rise in threats and abuse directed towards the nation's elected officials in recent years.
The independent lawmaker, 65, was getting things from the trunk of her car when she was struck by a Toyota Land Cruiser on Monday afternoon.
The driver had made a U-turn to get back to her after passing, Albanese said on Tuesday.
"It's clear this was a deliberate act," he said.
- 'TARGETED' ATTACK -
Haines was critically injured and underwent surgery overnight at the Alfred hospital in Melbourne.
National broadcaster ABC and The Sydney Morning Herald said that she had lost a leg, with reports indicating she was fighting to keep the other.
The 43-year-old male driver of the vehicle has been identified by Australian media and was reportedly known to police.

He was charged on Tuesday evening with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.
"Police will allege the incident was targeted," Victoria police said.

A statement released by the charged man's parents said Haines had been their friend for more than two decades and described Monday's events as "devastating and unfathomable", The Age newspaper reported.
"We would like to sincerely thank members of the local community and police who came to Helen's aid yesterday after the shocking and horrific crime," the statement said.
The alleged attacker was restrained by local barber Ricky Jefferies, now widely hailed as a "hero."
Jefferies told journalists his first thought had been: "My wife would be disappointed if I'm injured."
"My family, they're everything, and my community is second to that," a visibly shaken Jefferies told journalists.
"The other people here were just, they did so much more than me... they deserve the credit."

The alleged attacker's motive remains unknown and Albanese has refused to speculate while the investigation takes place.

"It's important in a democracy that people are allowed to have disagreements," he said.
"But that doesn't mean that you have to draw into question people's motivations or their patriotism or who they are."
"We've seen, I think, political discourse go in the wrong direction in recent times," he said.
Australia's spy agency chief Mike Burgess said "elevated levels of grievance, intolerance and polarisation continue to create a permissive environment of violence."

Tributes to her have poured in from across the political spectrum.--AFP

0cf94a2f7a96e4cd: TAIPEI: Chinese coast guard patrols to the east of Taiwan are "highly destabilising" and an extension of Beijing's legal, political and information warfare against Taipei, the chair of a review commission appointed by the US Congress said on Tuesday.
China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island's east coast since June with regular coast guard patrols.
China recognises no claims of sovereignty by Taiwan, including over the seas around the island.
Officials in Taiwan, which rejects Beijing's territorial claims, say they believe China is practising for a possible maritime blockade using overlapping military, paramilitary and civilian assets.

Speaking at a forum in Taipei, Randall Schriver, chair of the US Congress' US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, said one of the most troubling recent developments he had seen was the idea of a persistent coast guard patrol east of Taiwan.
While an ostensibly civilian vessel performing law enforcement duties could seem benign, in fact it is an extension of China's sovereignty claim, he added.
"This is an extension of legal warfare and political and information warfare. This is highly destabilising if they continue to operationalise this law enforcement role," he said.
China's foreign ministry reiterated comments from last week that those waters were Chinese and it was "therefore legitimate, lawful and beyond reproach for China to carry out activities" there.
Speaking at the same event, National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu said China had no legal claim to the waters off the island's east.
Later on Tuesday, Taiwan's defence ministry reported China carrying out another "joint combat readiness patrol" near the island with 27 military aircraft, including nuclear-capable H-6 bombers.
The US is Taiwan's most important international backer and arms supplier, despite a lack of formal diplomatic ties.

However, US president Donald Trump has yet to approve a new US$14 billion arms package for Taiwan, saying in May after meeting Chinese president Xi Jinping in Beijing that such sales were a "very good negotiating chip". In December, Trump approved US$11 billion of arms for Taiwan.
Schriver, a former US assistant secretary of defense, said Trump overall had a good record on approving weapons sales to Taiwan and providing military training.

"However, with Trump and Xi most likely due to meet twice more this year, at the Apec summit in China and the G20 in Florida, there would probably only be movement on the new package next year," he added.
"I think they'll find a way, whether it's splitting the package up or reimagining some of it as DCS or FMS," Schriver said, referring to direct commercial sales and foreign military sales.
"And I know that the support is there again in Congress and from much of the bureaucracy," he said.

4775b1c0b0133fdf: Microsoft has been forced to admit that the Always On VPN glitch – which it said it had fixed in an update on October 13 – was not actually fixed after all.

We've all been there. You fix that bug, or tweak the configuration setting, and you're pleased with yourself, but it turns out it didn't take, and you have to send the "er, about that fix" follow-up email of shame.

The same has happened to Microsoft. After proudly declaring the problem resolved as part of its last security update, the company had to roll back its triumphant trumpeting to a sad little parp from a clown's horn in the message WI1482218:
"This disclosure was mistakenly updated to Resolved status on October 13, 2026. We have returned its status to Mitigated.
"We apologize for any inconvenience or confusion."

The bug in question concerns the operating system's Always On VPN functionality, a useful bit of code that quietly opens a VPN connection in the background without tiresome prompts for authentication. It dates back to Windows 10, and Microsoft alerted administrators to problems after the September 2026 Windows security update inadvertently broke it.
The issue affects Windows 11 versions from 24H2 through 26H2.

The problem could occur when the VPN was set to try a different connection method if the initial connection failed (Microsoft gave the example of using automatic protocol selection with IKEv2 and SSTP).

According to Microsoft: "Affected VPN connections might remain in a 'Connecting' state or repeatedly attempt to connect without succeeding. Subsequent connection attempts might also display the error: 'The specified port is already in use'."

This is not ideal for administrators. The workaround Microsoft highlighted back on October 13 was to change from automatic protocol selection to a single protocol, which would at least get affected users up and running.
The workaround remains the same. The bad news is that, because last week's fix did not work, affected administrators will need to apply the workaround for a bit longer.
Microsoft claimed, "A resolution for this issue is planned to be included in an update to be released in the coming weeks." ®

f17af089ec83fcd0: RANTAU PANJANG: After 10 years in the police force, a corporal never imagined that a routine anti-drug operation would turn life-threatening when a suspect armed with a parang slashed his left arm.

"The suspect and his mother were at the house when we arrived.

The corporal said he and his colleagues chased the suspect for about 1km before the man turned on him.
"We approached him, believing he was about to surrender.

The corporal said it was the first time in his decade-long career that he had faced a life-threatening situation while on duty.
"I am now stable and have been discharged from hospital, but I still need follow-up treatment," he said.
acbe750e5f085a17: WASHINGTON: One-third of Americans think the government should try a second time to put a convicted criminal to death if a first execution attempt fails, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee.

The four-day poll, completed on Monday, showed 39% of respondents thought the government should instead allow convicts to serve life in prison following a failed execution, while 26% were not sure which was a better approach.

The nationwide survey found minority public support for trying again to execute inmates who survive execution attempts, a question Tennessee now faces after Christa Pike, 50, survived two lethal injection attempts last month in Nashville.

The convicted murderer was taken to a hospital unconscious following the attempted execution, critically ill and with severe arm injuries after two syringes of the caustic barbiturate pentobarbital failed to kill her, marking Tennessee's second botched lethal injection this year. She did not regain consciousness until five days later.

Most countries around the world, along with 23 US states, have abolished capital punishment. Those US states that still impose it have struggled in recent years to obtain execution drugs, and some have considered other methods, including firing squads.

A slight majority of Americans — 55% — continue to support capital punishment for people convicted of the most serious crimes, down from 63% who said in a 2017 Reuters/Ipsos poll that they supported the policy. Some 31% of respondents in the latest poll said they opposed the death penalty, while 13% either did not know or did not answer the question.
The issue has taken on new significance as courts consider whether states can make a second execution attempt after a failed one.

The US Supreme Court recently allowed a state to proceed with scheduling a second execution date after a failed attempt. Kenneth Smith, convicted of a 1988 murder-for-hire, survived a trip to Alabama's execution chamber in 2022 after prison officials failed to set up intravenous lines. But Alabama succeeded on its second try in 2024 with a new method of suffocation using nitrogen gas.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth recently floated the prospect of the first-ever livestream of a US execution, the planned death by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, the former US Army major who killed 13 people at Texas' Fort Hood military base.
Following widespread criticism – including from Republican lawmakers – President Donald Trump canceled the livestream plans, though officials still intend to carry out the execution on Dec 3.

Some 46% of Americans, including 29% of Democrats and 71% of Republicans, said it was appropriate to execute Hasan by firing squad. But 71% of people surveyed, including majorities of Democrats and Republicans, said showing executions to the public on television or the internet was inappropriate.
The Reuters/Ipsos poll was conducted online and nationwide, gathering responses from 1,679 US adults. It had a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

dd88aa55720af9a8: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Police have opened an investigation into the circulation of a podcast video alleging that drug trafficking activities were taking place at a house of worship near the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD) here.

Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the investigation was being conducted under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
